questions.q: DO NOW Q1 — name the three types of nuclear radiation.
DO NOW Q2 — which radiation is stopped by paper?

reveal.question: Name three natural sources of background radiation.

learn.heading: LEARN 1 — Atomic structure
learn.body:
Protons are positive.
Neutrons are neutral.
Electrons are negative.

learn.heading: LEARN 2 — Isotopes
learn.body:
Same protons, different neutrons.
Same element, different mass number.

learn.heading: LEARN 3 — Alpha decay
learn.body:
Emits a helium nucleus.
Mass number falls by 4, atomic number by 2.

learn.heading: LEARN 4 — Beta decay
learn.body:
A neutron becomes a proton.
An electron is emitted.
Atomic number rises by 1.

learn.heading: LEARN 5 — Gamma decay (SHOULD BE DROPPED past the 4-cap)
learn.body:
High-energy EM wave.
No change to mass or atomic number.

learn.heading: LEARN 6 — Half-life (SHOULD BE DROPPED past the 4-cap)
learn.body:
Time for half the nuclei to decay.
Constant for a given isotope.

build.q: BUILD MCQ 1 — which radiation is most ionising?
build.explanation: Alpha is the most ionising (and least penetrating).

build.q: BUILD MCQ 2 — which is stopped by a few mm of aluminium?
build.explanation: Beta is stopped by a few mm of aluminium.

build.q: BUILD MCQ 3 — what does gamma need to stop it?
build.explanation: Gamma needs thick lead or concrete.

build.q: BUILD MCQ 4 — isotopes of an element have the same number of what?

build.instruction: BUILD SORT (extra Build item) — sort each into penetrating power.

statements.text: Alpha radiation is the most penetrating.

statements.correction: Gamma does not change mass or atomic number.

statements.text: Beta decay emits a helium nucleus.
Isotopes differ in their number of protons.
statements.correction: Isotopes differ in NEUTRONS; protons are the same.

build.question: BUILD MARK-THE-ANSWERS — Explain why alpha radiation is dangerous if a source is swallowed but relatively safe outside the body.
build.instruction: Mark each answer. Give a level and a mark out of 6.

levelDescriptors.desc: Links high ionisation + short range to inside vs outside the body.

indicativeContent.text: It has a very short range / is stopped by skin.
Outside the body it cannot penetrate the skin.
Inside the body it damages cells directly.

doesNotAward: Alpha is the most penetrating (it is the least penetrating).
Alpha travels a long way in air.

samples.label: Student A
samples.text: Alpha is really penetrating so it goes right through you and thats why its dangerous inside.
samples.comment: Core misconception: alpha is the LEAST penetrating.

samples.label: Student B
samples.text: Alpha is strongly ionising but has a short range so outside the body the skin stops it, while inside it damages cells directly.

samples.label: Student C
samples.text: Its dangerous inside because there is more of it in your body.

developing.q: APPLY DEV 1 — name the radiation stopped by paper.
APPLY DEV 2 — what is an isotope?
developing.a: Atoms of the same element with different numbers of neutrons.

developing.q: APPLY DEV 3 — which radiation is an EM wave?

reaching.q: APPLY REA 1 — describe what happens to the nucleus in alpha decay.
reaching.a: It loses 2 protons and 2 neutrons (a helium nucleus).

reaching.q: APPLY REA 2 — a source has a half-life of 6 hours. What fraction remains after 18 hours?
APPLY REA 3 — explain why beta decay increases the atomic number.
reaching.a: A neutron turns into a proton, so proton number rises by 1.

mastering.q: APPLY MAS 1 — evaluate the use of gamma vs alpha sources for a medical tracer.
mastering.a: Gamma penetrates out of the body to be detected and is less ionising to tissue; alpha would be absorbed and cause damage.

mastering.q: APPLY MAS 2 — explain why background radiation must be subtracted from count-rate measurements.
mastering.a: Background adds counts not from the source, so the measured rate is too high unless corrected.

mastering.q: APPLY MAS 3 — a nuclide undergoes alpha then beta decay. Describe the net change in atomic number.
mastering.a: Alpha lowers Z by 2, beta raises Z by 1, so net change is -1.
